mainTopic: Far-away witnesses and doubtful קידושין, רב's list of offenses that earn מלקות, and רבא's rule about silence after the money is given
overview: This amud finishes the story of a woman betrothed with an item that was not worth a פרוטה where the קידושין happened, though it may have been worth a פרוטה in אידית. רב חסדא rules that she is not מקודשת. He says witnesses who are far away do not count, and he brings support from רבי חייא's wife יהודית and from רבי חנינא's ruling about a שבויה. אביי ורבא disagree, and in practice the רבנן avoided marrying into that woman's family because they held like אביי ורבא. Next comes a man who betrothed with a myrtle branch in the marketplace. רב יוסף ruled that he gets מלקות like רב and that a גט is needed like שמואל. This leads to רב's list of improper behaviors he punished, and to the view of the Sages of נהרדעא that רב flogged only for קידושין through ביאה. Finally, רבא rules that a woman's silence after the money is already given means nothing. He proves this from a ברייתא about a coin given as a deposit, and the גמרא begins to ask what 'she wanted' means there, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The story of יהודית, wife of רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא supports his ruling with a story. יהודית told רבי חייא that her mother said she had been betrothed as a child, and רבי חייא answered that her mother cannot forbid her to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this not like the case of יהודית, the wife of רבי חייא? She suffered painful childbirths. She told him: 'My mother told me that when I was young, my father accepted קידושין for me.' He answered her: 'Your mother does not have the power to forbid you to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a story to support his ruling that this woman is not treated as מקודשת. In the story, a claim that a woman was already betrothed is ignored because it is not backed up properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודית wanted out of the marriage because childbirth was so painful for her. If her mother's report were accepted, she would be an אשת איש and forbidden to רבי חייא. רבי חייא ruled that her mother's word alone cannot create that איסור. רב חסדא uses this to show that a possible earlier קידושין is not counted unless it is properly established in front of us.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this not the same as? (a phrase used to bring support from a similar case)
it is not in her power

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא is not calling her mother a liar. He is saying that her mother's word alone is not enough to make his wife forbidden to him.

phrases.english: Is this not like the case of Yehudit,
the wife of Rabbi Chiyya,
who had painful childbirths?
phrases.notes: Some versions say דַּהֲוֵית and some say דַּהֲוָה. The meaning is the same either way: she suffered pain in childbirth.

phrases.english: She said to him: My mother told me:
Your father accepted betrothal on your behalf
when you were young.
phrases.notes: She is telling him what her mother said to her, so 'your father' here means her own father.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: לָאו כָּל כְּמִינַּהּ דְּאִימָּךְ
phrases.english: He said to her: It is not in your mother's power
to forbid you to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו הַיְינוּ דִּיהוּדִית דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's ruling, which was stated just before this section
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that the woman is not treated as מקודשת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ruling that the mother's report of an earlier קידושין does not forbid his wife to him

steps.title: The רבנן point to witnesses in אידית
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רב חסדא why he ignores the fact that there are witnesses in אידית who know the item was worth a פרוטה that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב חסדא: Why do you rule this way? There are witnesses in אידית who know that on that day the item was worth a פרוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רב חסדא's ruling. They say there is real evidence, in another place, that the item was worth a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יהודית story, the only evidence was the mother's word. Here, the רבנן argue, the case is stronger because actual witnesses exist who know the item was worth a פרוטה. If so, the קידושין should take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of a place where the item was worth more
worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that can be used for קידושין

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב חִסְדָּא: אַמַּאי?
phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Chisda: Why?
After all, there are witnesses in Idit
who know that on that day
it was worth a peruta!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the item the man used for the קידושין in the earlier case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב חִסְדָּא: אַמַּאי? הָא אִיכָּא סָהֲדִי בְּאִידִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling that the step before supported
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that the woman is not מקודשת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses exist who know the item was worth a פרוטה, so the קידושין should be valid.

steps.title: The witnesses are not here now
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that, whatever those witnesses know, they are not here in front of us right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, in any case, they are not here in front of us.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge. Witnesses who are somewhere else do not count for the case we are deciding now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not deny that the witnesses exist. His point is that בית דין rules only on the evidence in front of it. Far-away witnesses are treated as if they were not there.

phrases.english: Now, in any case,
they are not here in front of us.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא לָא לֵיתַנְהוּ קַמַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits which evidence counts: only witnesses who are present matter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses anywhere in the world who know the value should make the קידושין valid
steps.terutzMaskana: We rule only on what is in front of us, and witnesses who are not here do not count
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core idea behind רב חסדא's view, and it is the idea that אביי ורבא will reject at the end of this section.

steps.title: Support from רבי חנינא: far-away witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא supports his answer with רבי חנינא's ruling that a woman is not forbidden just because her witnesses are far away in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this not the view of רבי חנינא? For רבי חנינא said: Her witnesses are far away in the north, and should she be forbidden?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a ruling from רבי חנינא to show that witnesses who are far away are ignored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's case is about a שבויה, a woman who was taken captive. Witnesses to her captivity who are far away do not affect how we treat her now. רב חסדא says the same applies here: the witnesses in אידית are far away, so they do not count.

keyTerms.meaning: the north, meaning a far-away place

phrases.english: Isn't this the view of Rabbi Chanina?
For Rabbi Chanina said:
Her witnesses are in the north, and shall she be forbidden?!
phrases.notes: He is talking about a woman who was taken captive. The witnesses to her captivity are far away, so we do not forbid her because of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's answer in the step before
steps.raayaObject: The rule that witnesses who are not present do not count
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's ruling about a שבויה whose witnesses are far away

steps.title: אביי ורבא disagree: a captive woman is a more lenient case
steps.stepSummary: אביי ורבא reject רב חסדא's view. Being lenient with a שבויה, who works to protect herself from her captor, does not mean we can be lenient with an אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי ורבא do not agree with this view of רב חסדא. If the חכמים were lenient with a שבויה, who makes herself repulsive to her captor, should we then be lenient with an אשת איש?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי ורבא reject רב חסדא's proof from רבי חנינא. They say the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבויה usually makes herself look repulsive so her captor will leave her alone, so there was already a reason to be lenient with her. An אשת איש is a very serious איסור, and no special reason for leniency exists. So רבי חנינא's leniency cannot be extended to the case of קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: they do not hold this view
a woman who was taken captive

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: we judge only by what is in front of us, so far-away witnesses do not count, and he learns this from רבי חנינא's ruling about a שבויה. אביי ורבא: we cannot learn from a שבויה, which is a lenient case, to an אשת איש, which is a serious איסור.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava do not hold
in accordance with this ruling of Rav Chisda.
If they were lenient with a captive woman,
who makes herself repulsive to her captor,
shall we be lenient with a married woman?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא לָא סְבִירָא לְהוּ לְהָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רבי חנינא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both רב חסדא's ruling and his proof from רבי חנינא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שבויה case had its own reason for leniency, which does not apply to the serious איסור of אשת איש

steps.title: The rabbis kept away from that family, following אביי ורבא
steps.stepSummary: Descendants of the woman's family stayed in סורא, and the רבנן did not marry into it. The reason was not that they followed שמואל. It was that they followed אביי ורבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of that family remained in סורא, and the רבנן kept away from it. This was not because they held like שמואל. It was because they held like אביי ורבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how the earlier case ended in real life: the רבנן avoided marrying into the woman's family. It also tells us exactly which opinion made them act this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman had remarried without a גט, so if her first betrothal was valid, her children could be ממזרים. The גמרא says the רבנן were worried because of אביי ורבא's point in Step 5 that witnesses in another place still count. It was not because of שמואל's broader worry that any item might be worth a פרוטה somewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: they kept away from it (did not marry into it)

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the רבנן were stricter than רב חסדא. They followed אביי ורבא: witnesses who know the item's value, even if they are far away, are enough to make us worry the betrothal was real.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two strict opinions. שמואל worries that the item might be worth a פרוטה somewhere. אביי ורבא worry because actual witnesses exist in another place. The גמרא says the רבנן acted for the second reason only.

phrases.english: Some of that family remained in Sura,
phrases.notes: This is the family of the woman from רב חסדא's case. She remarried, and her descendants lived in סורא.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis kept away from it.
And it was not because they held like Shmuel,
phrases.notes: שמואל worried that the item might be worth a פרוטה in some other place.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דִּסְבִירָא לְהוּ כְּאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא.
phrases.english: rather, because they held like Abaye and Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִשּׁוּם דִּסְבִירָא לְהוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דִּסְבִירָא לְהוּ כְּאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the practical outcome followed אביי ורבא's rejection of רב חסדא in Step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן avoided the family because they held like אביי ורבא: witnesses in another place must be taken into account.

steps.title: A man betrothed with a myrtle branch in the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace. רב אחא בר הונא sent the case to רב יוסף and asked what the law is.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace. רב אחא בר הונא sent the question to רב יוסף: in a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new real-life case and asks a question about it. This sets up רב יוסף's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two problems are mixed together here. First, a myrtle branch may not be worth a פרוטה, so it is unclear whether the betrothal works at all. Second, betrothing in a public marketplace is improper behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: in a case like this, what is the law?

phrases.english: A certain man who betrothed a woman
with a myrtle branch in the marketplace,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁלְחַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Huna sent it before Rav Yosef:
In a case like this, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁלְחַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף: כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about a betrothal item of doubtful value
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the law is for a betrothal done with a myrtle branch in the marketplace

steps.title: רב יוסף: flog him like רב, require a גט like שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answered: give the man מלקות, following רב, and require a גט, following שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: Flog him, like רב. And require a גט, like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question with two rulings. One punishes the man's behavior, and the other deals with whether the woman is married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flogging him follows רב, who punished improper ways of betrothing. Requiring a גט follows שמואל: the myrtle branch might be worth a פרוטה somewhere else, so the betrothal might be real and must be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: flog him (give him מכת מרדות, rabbinic lashes)

steps.whyThisMatters: Here שמואל's worry about the item's value elsewhere is applied in practice. It is used to be strict and require a גט.

phrases.english: He sent to him:
Flog him, in accordance with Rav,
and require a bill of divorce, in accordance with Shmuel.
phrases.notes: The branch might be worth a פרוטה somewhere else, so the betrothal might have worked.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: נַגְּדֵיהּ כְּרַב, וְאַצְרֵיךְ גִּיטָּא כִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man gets מלקות following רב, and the woman needs a גט following שמואל

steps.title: רב flogged men for improper ways of betrothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reference to רב. He would flog a man who betrothed in the marketplace, through relations, or without an arrangement first.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב would flog a man who betroths in the marketplace, a man who betroths through relations, and a man who betroths without arranging it first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what 'like רב' meant in Step 8. It starts listing the behaviors רב punished, beginning with improper ways of betrothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list explains why the man in our case was flogged: he betrothed in the marketplace, which is on רב's list. All three items are legal ways to betroth that are done in an improper manner.

keyTerms.meaning: relations (one of the ways to betroth)
an arrangement, talking it over before betrothing

steps.confusionAlert: The betrothal still works in these cases. רב is punishing the improper way it was done, not saying the קידושין is invalid.

phrases.english: For Rav would flog one who betroths in the marketplace,
and one who betroths through relations,
and one who betroths without an arrangement.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב מְנַגֵּיד עַל דִּמְקַדֵּשׁ בְּשׁוּקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'like רב' part of רב יוסף's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב gives מלקות for betrothing in the marketplace, through relations, or without an arrangement first

steps.title: More things רב flogged for: cancelling a גט, disrespecting the rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The list continues. רב also flogged a man who cancels a גט, who issues a declaration against a גט, who torments a messenger of the רבנן, or who stays in שמתא for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב also flogged: a man who cancels a גט, a man who makes a declaration against a גט, a man who torments a messenger of the רבנן, and a man who has a שמתא on him for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps listing behaviors that רב punished. The list now moves beyond betrothal to divorce and to respect for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cancelling a גט or secretly declaring it forced can lead a woman to think she is divorced when she is not. Mistreating the רבנן's messenger, or staying under a שמתא for thirty days without fixing it, shows disrespect for the בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: cancels a גט he already sent
a declaration that a coming act is forced and not truly meant
a messenger of the רבנן (of the בית דין)

phrases.english: and one who nullifies a bill of divorce,
and one who issues a declaration about a bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: He says beforehand that he is giving the גט against his will. That makes the גט not work.

phrases.english: and one who torments a messenger of the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דְּחָלָה שַׁמְתָּא עִילָּוֵיהּ תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין,
phrases.english: and one who had a ban rest upon him for thirty days,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דִּמְבַטֵּיל גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of behaviors רב punished
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב gives מלקות for cancelling a גט, issuing a declaration against a גט, tormenting a messenger of the רבנן, and staying in שמתא for thirty days

steps.title: A son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house
steps.stepSummary: The list of people רב flogged ends with a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב also flogged a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the last item to רב's list from the earlier steps. Living in the father-in-law's house was also something רב punished with מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living in the same house as his mother-in-law puts a son-in-law in an improper situation, so רב punished it. The wording says 'lives there,' and the next step will question exactly that word.

phrases.english: And for a son-in-law
who lives in his father-in-law's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל חַתְנָא דְּדָיַיר בֵּי חֲמוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in the list of offenses רב flogged for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב flogged a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house.

steps.title: Why was a son-in-law who only passed by flogged?
steps.stepSummary: The wording suggests only living there is punished, but רב ששת flogged a son-in-law who only walked past the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he lives there, yes, but if he only passes by, no? But there was a son-in-law who passed by the door of his father-in-law's house, and רב ששת flogged him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording 'who lives there.' It points to a story where רב ששת gave מלקות to a son-in-law who only walked past.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'lives there' implies that just passing by is fine. The story about רב ששת seems to contradict that, since he punished someone for less.

phrases.english: One who lives there — yes,
one who passes by — no?!
But there was that son-in-law
who passed by the door of his father-in-law's house
and רב ששת flogged him!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּדָיַיר – אִין, חָלֵיף – לָא?! וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of the word דדייר in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that only living in the house is punished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story shows רב ששת flogged a son-in-law who only passed by.

steps.title: That case already had rumors
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's case was special because there were already rumors about the son-in-law and his mother-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case, there was a rumor going around about his mother-in-law and him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב ששת's case was unusual. Rumors already connected the man and his mother-in-law, so even walking by was a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only living there is punished. When rumors already exist, even passing by feeds them, so it deserves מלקות. The general rule stays the same, and this case is an exception because of its special facts.

phrases.english: That one — there was something
rumored about his mother-in-law with him.
phrases.notes: He means people were already whispering about the two of them, so walking by made it worse.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מֵידָם הֲוָת דָּיְימָא חֲמָתֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת flogged anyone who simply passed by.
steps.terutzMaskana: Passing by is punished only where rumors already existed.

steps.title: נהרדעא: רב flogged only for ביאה without a שידוך
steps.stepSummary: The Sages of נהרדעא say רב did not flog for everything on the list, only for קידושין through ביאה without an arrangement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages of נהרדעא say: in all of these cases רב did not flog, except for one who betroths through relations without an arrangement.
steps.whatsHappening: A different tradition makes רב's list much shorter. It says רב flogged for only one thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9–11 gave a long list. נהרדעא says רב actually flogged only for קידושין through ביאה when there was no שידוך first. That means a planned ביאה would not be punished.

keyTerms.meaning: marital relations, here used as a way to make קידושין

phrases.english: The Sages of נהרדעא say:
In all of these, רב did not flog,
except for one who betroths through relations
without an arrangement.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהַרְדָּעֵי אָמְרִי: בְּכוּלְּהוּ, לָא מְנַגֵּיד רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different tradition that narrows רב's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב flogged only for קידושין through ביאה without a שידוך.

steps.title: Another version: even with a שידוך
steps.stepSummary: Some say that even with a שידוך, רב flogged for קידושין through ביאה because it is indecent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: even with an arrangement as well, because of indecency.
steps.whatsHappening: Another version of the נהרדעא tradition says רב flogged for any קידושין through ביאה, even when it was planned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the problem was the lack of a שידוך. In this version, the problem is the act itself, because making קידושין this way is פריצות. So a שידוך does not help.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions disagree only about whether a prior שידוך prevents רב's מלקות for קידושין through ביאה.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
even with an arrangement, he also flogged
because of indecency.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּשִׁידּוּכֵי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version that widens step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב flogged for קידושין through ביאה even with a שידוך, because it is פריצות.

steps.title: The myrtle mat with four זוזי inside
steps.stepSummary: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle mat. When told it was worth less than a פרוטה, he said to use the four זוזי inside it. She took it and was silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man betrothed a woman with a mat of myrtle. They told him it wasn't worth a פרוטה. He said: let her be betrothed with the four זוזי in it. She took it and was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about קידושין. It sets up a question for רבא: does her silence count as agreeing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first thing he gave was worth too little, so it could not make קידושין. He then named something valuable inside it. The woman never said yes; she just stayed quiet.

keyTerms.meaning: worth a פרוטה, the minimum value for קידושין

phrases.english: There was a certain man who betrothed
with a mat of myrtle,
phrases.notes: This is a new case, not the myrtle branch story from step 7.

phrases.english: They said to him:
But it is not worth a פרוטה!
He said to them:
Let her be betrothed with the four זוזי that are in it.
She took it and was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּקַדֵּישׁ בְּצִיפְּתָא דְאָסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a case of קידושין with an item worth too little.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: a woman took the item silently after the man changed what he was betrothing her with.

steps.title: רבא: silence after the money is given means nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that silence after the money was already handed over does not count as agreeing, so she is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is silence after the money was given, and any silence after the money was given is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא decides the myrtle mat case. Her silence does not show that she accepted קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she took the mat, it was worth too little to make קידושין. He named the four זוזי only after she already had it. Staying quiet at that point does not prove she agreed, so it counts for nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying silence never counts. He is saying silence AFTER the money was already handed over is not enough to show she agreed.

phrases.english: רבא said:
This is silence after the giving of the money,
and any silence
that comes after the giving of the money
is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָוֵה שְׁתִיקוּתָא דִּלְאַחַר מַתַּן מָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Silence after the money was handed over has no legal effect; she is not betrothed.

steps.title: רבא's proof: the deposit ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: if a coin given as a deposit is later declared קידושין, she is betrothed only if she wants to be.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: how do I know this? A ברייתא teaches: he said to her, 'Take this סלע as a deposit,' and then said, 'Be betrothed to me with it.' If he said it while giving the money, she is betrothed. If he said it after giving the money, then if she wanted, she is betrothed, and if she did not want, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports his ruling with a ברייתא. A declaration of קידושין made after the money is already in her hands needs her real agreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that when the declaration came after the money was given, she is betrothed only if 'she wanted.' רבא reads this as proof that her silence at that point does not count. The next steps work out what 'she wanted' and 'she did not want' mean, which is where the proof gets its force.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say this?

steps.whatToRemember: A declaration of קידושין made after the money is already given works only if the woman actively wants it; silence is not enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule for קידושין: her agreement must be clear when the money and the words do not come together.

phrases.english: רבא said: From where do I say this?
As it is taught: he said to her:
Take this סלע as a deposit,
and then he went back and said to her:
Be betrothed to me with it.
If at the time of giving the money, she is betrothed,
if after giving the money,
if she wanted, she is betrothed,
if she did not want, she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for רבא's ruling in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that silence after the money is given has no effect.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a סלע given as a deposit and later declared קידושין, which works only if she wanted it.

steps.title: What do 'she wanted' and 'she did not want' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of the two terms in the ברייתא: 'she wanted' and 'she did not want'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'she wanted' mean, and what does 'she did not want' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the ברייתא means by 'she wanted' and 'she did not want'. This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that if a coin was given as a deposit and later declared קידושין, she is betrothed only if 'she wanted'. The גמרא needs to know what counts as wanting. Does she have to say yes out loud, or is something else enough? The answer decides how strongly the ברייתא supports רבא's ruling about silence.

keyTerms.meaning: She did not want (she did not agree)

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'she wanted'?
And what is the meaning of 'she did not want'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״רָצְתָה״ וּמַאי ״לֹא רָצְתָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the key terms mean in the ברייתא brought in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What level of agreement 'she wanted' requires, and what 'she did not want' refers to.

steps.title: Testing the reading that 'wanted' means saying yes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'she wanted' means she said yes and 'she did not want' means she said no. It then starts to draw an inference about the first clause of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that 'she wanted' means she said 'yes', and 'she did not want' means she said 'no', then you can infer that in the first clause...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a simple reading: wanting means saying 'yes' and not wanting means saying 'no'. Then it begins to show what this reading would imply for the first part of the ברייתא. The sentence is not finished on this amud and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אִילֵימָא ('if you say') signals a possible reading that the גמרא is about to knock down. The first clause of the ברייתא covers a case where he spoke at the moment he gave the money, and it does not mention her wanting at all. If the second clause is about an outright 'no', the first clause would have to include her saying 'no' too. The גמרא is building toward that difficult result.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading the גמרא will usually reject)
By inference; it follows from this
The first clause of a source

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final explanation. אִילֵימָא introduces a suggestion that is being set up to be challenged.

phrases.english: If we say 'she wanted' means that she said 'yes',
and 'she did not want' means that she said 'no',
then by inference, in the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the case where he spoke as he handed her the money. The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא ״רָצְתָה״ – דְּאָמְרָה: ״אִין״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in Step 19 and starts testing it against the ברייתא's first clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'she wanted' means she said 'yes' and 'she did not want' means she said 'no'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the second clause contrasts an explicit yes with an explicit no, the first clause would imply that she is betrothed in every case, even if she said no. The challenge is completed on the next amud.
